title: Death at Gull Rock Lighthouse
setting: Gull Rock Lighthouse, a remote island station cut off by a storm on the night of 14 November.
victim: Harold Voss, the lighthouse keeper, found dead at the foot of the lamp-room stairs at 06:00 with a head wound.
briefing: Harold Voss was killed between 23:00 and 01:00 while the storm kept everyone on the island. The lamp went dark at about 23:40 and was relit at 00:15. Three people were on the rock that night. One of them killed him.

suspects.name: Mara Quill
suspects.publicStatement: I was sheltering in my boat at the jetty all night. I never went near the tower.
suspects.persona: Blunt, weathered woman in her fifties who answers questions with questions when nervous. Speaks in short sentences.
suspects.secret: She has been smuggling untaxed brandy to the island for years and Harold had never reported it.
suspects.alibi: Claims she stayed in her boat's cabin at the jetty from 22:00 until dawn, alone.
knows: At about 00:25 she saw Edwin Pike walking from the tower toward the oil store, carrying a lantern, which she found odd in the storm.
She heard Harold shout angrily at someone near the tower door a little before the lamp went dark.
Edwin told her at supper that he never goes out after dark because of his bad knee.
Harold asked her to carry a letter to the mainland about fraud in the station's fuel accounts.

suspects.name: Edwin Pike
suspects.publicStatement: I turned in at ten with a bad knee and slept through it all. I heard nothing.
suspects.persona: Polite, precise, slightly pompous man in his forties who speaks formally and never raises his voice.
suspects.secret: Harold was about to expose that Edwin falsified the logbook and fuel records and sold the spare oil on the mainland.
suspects.alibi: Claims he went to bed at 22:00 in the keepers' quarters and did not wake until the alarm at 06:00.
knows: He is the killer: he struck Harold with the brass lamp key after Harold confronted him about the fuel records, then relit the lamp at 00:15.
His boots and oilskin were wet and muddy when he washed up, and he hid the brass lamp key in the oil store.
He knows Harold told him that evening he would report the fuel thefts to the Lighthouse Board on the next boat.

suspects.name: Tess Harrow
suspects.publicStatement: I cleaned the kitchen, went to my room at eleven and stayed there. Poor Harold.
suspects.persona: Warm, chatty woman in her sixties who rambles and calls everyone dear.
suspects.secret: She has been secretly reading Harold's private letters from his estranged daughter because she was worried about him.
suspects.alibi: Says she was in her room off the kitchen from 23:00, awake with a toothache, until the morning.
knows: From her window at about 23:15 she saw Edwin Pike crossing the yard toward the tower in his oilskin, with a lantern.
At about 00:20 she saw the lamp burning again and a man's shape come back from the tower; the lamp had been dark before that.
Edwin has been strangely cheerful about the fuel deliveries and nervous whenever Harold mentioned the logbook.
Harold told her that week he had found fraud in the fuel logbook and meant to report it.

motives.label: To stop Harold exposing his fraud

clues: Mud and wet oilskin fibres on the lamp-room stairs.
The brass lamp key, with traces of blood, hidden in the oil store.
The fuel ledger has pages torn out in Edwin's handwriting style.

solution.explanation: Edwin Pike falsified the fuel records and sold spare oil. Harold meant to report him, so Edwin killed him with the brass lamp key, relit the lamp at 00:15 and hid the key in the oil store. Mara and Tess both saw him outside with a lantern, contradicting his claim of sleeping all night.
